extraFacts.fact: 75% of a 10,000 psi full scale is 7,500 psi; 75% of 15,000 psi is 11,250 psi.

extraFacts.fact: Enerpac advises running a gauge at no more than about 75% of full scale in normal use, and recommends a gauge snubber or needle valve for high-cycle applications. A glycerine fill damps pointer flutter from pump pulsation and vibration.

faqs.q: What are Enerpac 2.5" glycerin-filled hydraulic pressure gauges used for?
faqs.a: Enerpac 2.5" gauges are glycerin-filled hydraulic pressure gauges with a lower or center rear mount, from 100 psi to 15,000 psi full scale. Fifteen part numbers are listed on the [pressure gauges shelf](/c/ic-pressure-gauges).

faqs.q: How do I read the Enerpac 2.5" gauge part numbers?
faqs.a: The G25 numbers step up with the range: G2509L is 0-100 psi, G2510L is 0-160 psi and G2536L is 0-15,000 psi. An R at the end, as in G2531R and G2538R, marks the center rear mount versions; the L numbers are lower mount.

faqs.q: Which pressure ranges does the Enerpac 2.5" gauge come in?
faqs.a: The ranges are 0-100, 0-160, 0-200, 0-300, 0-600, 0-1,000, 0-2,000, 0-3,000, 0-6,000, 0-10,000 and 0-15,000 psi. Pick a scale whose full reading is roughly twice the normal working pressure.

faqs.q: Which Enerpac 2.5" gauges have a center rear mount?
faqs.a: Four are listed with a center rear mount: G2531R (0-1,000 psi), G2534R (0-6,000 psi), G2537R (0-10,000 psi) and G2538R (0-15,000 psi). The rest mount from the lower connection.

faqs.q: Which fluid and pressure basis apply to the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges?
faqs.a: Gauge ranges are full-scale pressure readings, so choose a range well above the working pressure of the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges application; the pressure is read in psi, and the ranges listed are in the size table. Quote the range and connection you need.

faqs.q: Does Indus supply calibration documents with the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges?
faqs.a: No calibration certificate is listed for the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges. If your job needs a calibration or test report, ask for it on your [request](/contact) before ordering so we can confirm what is available.

faqs.q: What fittings connect the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges to a line?
faqs.a: Use fittings that match the gauge connection and the working pressure, such as the [instrumentation tube fittings](/c/instrumentation-tube-fittings); 15 part numbers are listed for the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges, for example G2509L, G2510L and G2511L.

faqs.q: How do I protect the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges in service?
faqs.a: Fit a snubber or needle valve where the line pulsates or runs high cycle, and choose a range roughly twice the working pressure so spikes stay on the scale. Mount the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges by its connection, not by the case; see the [glycerine-filled vs dry gauges guide](/blog/glycerine-filled-vs-dry-pressure-gauges).

faqs.q: Where is the Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges used?
faqs.a: The Enerpac 2.5" Glycerin-Filled Hydraulic Pressure Gauges are used on hydraulic power units, test benches and tooling lines where a local pressure reading is needed. See the [high-pressure hydraulic gauges guide](/blog/high-pressure-hydraulic-gauges) for pressure, force and digital gauges.

faqs.q: How does the Enerpac 2.5" gauge compare with the 4" G and H series?
faqs.a: The 2.5" gauges run from 100 to 15,000 psi, while the [4" gauges](/p/enerpac-4-in-glycerin-filled-hydraulic-pressure-gauges-g-and-high-cycle-h) cover 10,000 and 15,000 psi with 1/4" or 1/2" NPTF connections and add a dry high-cycle H-series.

faqs.q: What are Enerpac 4" G-series and H-series hydraulic pressure gauges used for?
faqs.a: They are 100 mm (4") lower-mount hydraulic pressure gauges in two builds. The glycerine-filled G-series goes to 10,000 and 15,000 psi and the dry H-series high-cycle gauges go to 10,000 psi, all with dual psi and bar scales; see the [pressure gauges shelf](/c/ic-pressure-gauges).

faqs.q: How do I read the Enerpac G40 and H40 part numbers?
faqs.a: The letter is the build: G4039L, G4088L, G4040L and G4089L are glycerine-filled G-series, and H4049L and H4071L are dry high-cycle H-series. The two connections are 1/4" NPTF and 1/2" NPTF, which the rows show per part number.

faqs.q: Which ranges and connections does the Enerpac 4" gauge come in?
faqs.a: Ranges are 0-10,000 psi and 0-15,000 psi, each with a 1/4" or 1/2" NPTF connection. G4088L and H4049L are 10,000 psi with 1/4" NPTF; G4039L and H4071L are 10,000 psi with 1/2" NPTF.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Enerpac G-series and H-series gauge?
faqs.a: The G-series is glycerine-filled and the H-series is dry. In the G-series the pressure-sensing parts are sealed and damped in glycerine, with a safety blow-out disc and pressure-equalising membrane. The H-series is dry and built for high-cycle work and harsh environments; Enerpac recommends a snubber or needle valve with both.

faqs.q: How much of full scale should an Enerpac gauge run at?
faqs.a: Enerpac advises running a gauge at no more than about 75% of full scale in normal use. So a 0-10,000 psi gauge suits a working pressure of about 7,500 psi or less.

faqs.q: What do GP10S and GP15S mean?

faqs.q: Which range of GP gauge should I pick?
faqs.a: Pick a scale whose full reading is roughly twice the normal working pressure, so the GP10S suits a working pressure up to about 5,000 psi; Enerpac advises running its gauges at no more than about 75% of full scale.

faqs.q: Which fluid and pressure basis apply to the Enerpac GP 4" Dry Pressure Gauges?

faqs.q: What fittings connect the Enerpac GP 4" Dry Pressure Gauges to a line?
